sections.label: Online vice arrests rise
sections.summary: The share of females arrested for online vice rose from 16% in 2015 to 55% in 2018, and seven in 10 foreign females arrested between 2015 and 2018 served in residential estates.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
sentences.text: To give a sense of how much online vice has grown in recent years: in 2015, the proportion of females arrested for online vice, compared to all types of platform, was 16%.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
sentences.text: In 2018, this proportion had increased to 55%.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
sentences.text: Another startling statistic: between 2015 and 2018, seven in 10 foreign females arrested for online vice were providing sexual services in residential estates.

sections.label: Syndicate earnings versus fines
sections.summary: A syndicate member can easily earn $100,000 a year, far exceeding the current maximum fine of $10,000.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
sentences.text: Today, a syndicate member can easily earn $100,000 in a year, and this far exceeds the current maximum fine of $10,000.

sections.label: Penalties for prostitution offences
sections.summary: Second or subsequent conviction carries up to seven years' jail, a $150,000 fine, or both, and living off prostitution earnings carries a mandatory jail term and discretionary fine.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
sentences.text: On second or subsequent conviction, a maximum jail term of seven years, or maximum fine of $150,000, or both.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
sentences.text: For the more serious offences, such as living off the earnings of prostitution under section 146, on first conviction, a mandatory jail term of up to seven years, and a discretionary maximum fine of $100,000.

sections.label: Deterring pop-up brothels
sections.summary: The third amendment promotes responsible lease of premises to deter pop-up brothels, which are rising especially in residential estates.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
sentences.text: The third amendment relates to promoting the responsible lease of premises, to deter "pop-up brothels". "Pop-up brothels" are on the rise, especially in residential estates.

sections.label: Liability for renting brothels
sections.summary: Clause 12 makes owners who rent out, or tenants who sublet, a place used as a brothel criminally liable unless they lacked knowledge and could not have ascertained it with reasonable diligence.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
sentences.text: For property owners and tenants, clause 12 amends section 148 subsections (3) and (4) such that: an owner who rents out, or a tenant who sublets, a place which is used as a brothel, will be criminally liable unless he or she can show that, at the time of entering into the letting of that place, he or she had no knowledge and could not, with reasonable diligence, have ascertained that the place was to be used as a brothel.

sections.label: Broadening brothel definition
sections.summary: Clause 2 broadens the definition of brothel to include any place advertised or represented as used for prostitution and likely to be so used.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
sentences.text: First, clause 2 broadens the definition of "brothel" to include any place that has been advertised or represented as being used for the purpose of prostitution and is likely to be used for the purpose of prostitution.

sections.label: Offence of harbouring for prostitution
sections.summary: Clause 3 amends section 140(1)(d) to make it an offence to bring into Singapore, receive or harbour any woman or girl for prostitution.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
sentences.text: Second, clause 3 amends section 140 subsection (1)(d) to make it clear that it is an offence for a person to bring into Singapore, receive or harbour any woman or girl for prostitution.

sections.label: Remote communication service sexual offences
sections.summary: Clause 10 changes section 146A to using a remote communication service for sexual service, and clause 15 extends arrest powers to that offence.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
sentences.text: Third, clause 10 amends section 146A to change the element of "operating or maintaining a remote communication service" for the provision of sexual service to that of "using" a remote communication service for that purpose.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
sentences.text: Lastly, clause 15 amends section 174 subsection (1) to extend the powers of arrest to the offence of using a remote communication service under section 146A.

sections.label: Reporting suspicious vice activities
sections.summary: The passage urges reporting suspicious neighbourhood activities to Police and greater vigilance to keep neighbourhoods safe and stop vice spreading.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
sentences.text: If we find any suspicious activities in the neighbourhood, do not hesitate to report to the Police immediately.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
sentences.text: If all of us can increase our vigilance and do our part, we will be able to keep our neighbourhoods safe and stop vice activities from spreading.

sections.label: Harsher punishments for vice syndicates
sections.summary: The passage says proposed regulations bring harsher punishments to syndicates and asks how the amendments help in Telegram group cases.

sentences.speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Hence, the proposed regulations to bring harsher punishments to such syndicates are timely.

sentences.speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: I note that the Police have arrested people in a Telegram group that was sharing obscene videos and photos of women.

sentences.speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Some media reports also alleged that independent sex workers, or perhaps even their syndicates, were advertising sexual services in the group.

sentences.speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: How will the amendments help in such cases?

sections.label: Enhanced penalties for vice syndicates
sections.summary: The passage states tenancy contracts must evolve and notes penalties will be enhanced to deter vice syndicates and those bringing foreigners for sex work.

sentences.speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Tenancy contracts will have to evolve to reflect this.

sentences.speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: I am pleased to note that penalties will be enhanced to deter vice syndicates who profit off their sex workers and those who bring in foreigners for sex work.

sections.label: Collaboration on apartment vice issues
sections.summary: The passage asks frontline agencies to be more sympathetic and collaborative, notes a unit was used as a brothel, and calls for recognition of community partners.

sentences.speaker: Prof Fatimah Lateef (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: But can the frontline agencies and officers not be more sympathetic, more understanding, more aligned and more collaborative in their responses in the handling of such issues from the community and the public?

sentences.speaker: Prof Fatimah Lateef (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: That unit in the narrative I shared amounted to being used as a brothel, aligning with all of its definitions in section 2 of this Bill, including the example on "circumstantial evidence".

sentences.speaker: Prof Fatimah Lateef (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: The use of apartment units for vice is very challenging.

sentences.speaker: Prof Fatimah Lateef (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: Thus, I am calling for greater recognition and collaboration with the community partners and residents living in specific areas.

sections.label: Enforcement consistency and HDB surveillance
sections.summary: Enforcement must be consistent to keep its intended impact, and HDB and residential premises need more surveillance, monitoring and proactive measures.

sentences.speaker: Prof Fatimah Lateef (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: Enforcement, as shared in this Bill, too, has to have consistency, or else it will lose the impact that is intended.

sentences.speaker: Prof Fatimah Lateef (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: Now, the review of Housing and Development Board (HDB) and residential premises need even more surveillance, monitoring and proactive measures.

sections.label: CEA dialogue and vice links
sections.summary: The speaker asks whether more can be worked out with CEA, HDB and MPs in focus groups, citing links between sex, drugs, scams and online vice.

sentences.speaker: Prof Fatimah Lateef (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: Can something more substantial be worked out with CEA as you are having a dialogue with them – HDB and, indeed, we are looking forward perhaps even to have Members of Parliament being engaged in your focus group discussions because we may have issues that may need to be addressed in some of these reviews?

sentences.speaker: Prof Fatimah Lateef (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: There is a stark link between sex, prostitution, sex drugs, sex enhancing drugs, drug utilisation and sales, love scams, online vice and even cigarette cartel.

sections.label: Coffee shop staircases and prostitution
sections.summary: The speaker asks whether authorities see that coffee shop staircases lead to upper units conducive to prostitution or illegal brothels.

sentences.speaker: Prof Fatimah Lateef (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: Is it not so obvious to the authorities?

sentences.speaker: Prof Fatimah Lateef (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: These coffee shops have got staircases leading to the upper units and these extremely conducive places for prostitution, or even to be used as an illegal brothel.

sections.label: Vice syndicates, MHA strategy, brothel definition
sections.summary: Vice syndicates use technology across borders, and the speaker asks MHA's strategy while supporting enhanced penalties and the widened brothel definition.

sentences.speaker: Prof Fatimah Lateef (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: Vice syndicates leverage technology to expand and flourish their operations, crossing borders even.

sentences.speaker: Prof Fatimah Lateef (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: What is MHA's strategy for tackling this efficiently and effectively?

sentences.speaker: Prof Fatimah Lateef (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: All in all, Sir, I support the enhanced penalties, and the amendment Bill must execute what it is intended to do to maintain the morality, rights and status of women.

sentences.speaker: Prof Fatimah Lateef (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: I hope to see the enhanced collaborative efforts clean up our heartlands and beyond.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: I welcome the changes to the definition of "brothel" to include what has been expressly or implicitly advertised or represented as being used for the purposes of prostitution.

sections.label: Hong Kong website listing women
sections.summary: A third incarnation of a well-known Hong Kong website currently lists 399 women providing vice activities in Singapore.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: The third incarnation of a well-known website from Hong Kong currently lists 399 women providing vice activities in Singapore.

sections.label: Hong Kong 2013 vice raid
sections.summary: When Hong Kong police raided the vice ring over three days in 2013, an estimated US$15 million in cash was seized.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: When the Hong Kong police conducted a three-day raid on the vice ring in 2013, an estimated US$15 million in cash was seized.

sections.label: Comparing penalties across related laws
sections.summary: The speaker urges the Charter be strengthened to match stronger deterrents in other laws, and other Acts amended if the Charter's penalties are stronger.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: How do they compare to penalties in other related laws, such as in the Prevention of Human Trafficking Act?

sentences.speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: I urge that where stronger deterrents are found in our other laws, that the Charter be further strengthened to match those, and, if the Charter provides for stronger penalties, then other related Acts be amended as well.

sections.label: Woman held captive in brothel
sections.summary: A woman held captive in a brothel in a neighbouring country serviced up to 15 clients a day and died of AIDS two months after being interviewed.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: Held captive in a brothel far away in a neighbouring country, she serviced up to 15 clients a day.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: By then, she had acquired immunodeficiency syndrome (AIDS) and passed away two months after I interviewed her.

sections.label: Abolishing prostitution in Singapore
sections.summary: The speaker asks that the Charter be amended to abolish prostitution in Singapore and urges greater bravery in eradicating exploitation of women.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: But those who are in this so-called oldest of "professions", whether in Singapore or elsewhere, are but a reflection of inequality and servitude that plagues our world.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: I would very much like to ask that the Charter be amended to abolish prostitution from Singapore.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: It is nothing but a stain upon the hard-earned rights of our Singapore women.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: I support the Bill's intent to strengthen the authorities’ hand in clamping down but I urge for greater bravery and gumption in eradicating the exploitation of women from our shores.

sections.label: Term mentally defective and penalty increase
sections.summary: The speaker asks the Minister to assure that 'mentally defective' is replaced with a dignified description and asks if raising the penalty from $10,000 to $100,000 will deter offenders.

sentences.speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Can the Minister please assure us that the term "mentally defective" will be replaced with a more appropriate and dignified description that does not perpetuate this persistent need to label them as inferior human beings?

sentences.speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: First, will increasing the present penalty of $10,000 to $100,000 be enough to deter the offenders?

sections.label: Pimps prosecuted versus sex workers arrested
sections.summary: The speaker asks the Minister for the number of pimps and vice-abettors prosecuted in the last three years versus sex workers arrested, and if the penalty increase is sufficient.

sentences.speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Could the Minister please share with the House what is the number of pimps and vice-abettors prosecuted in the last three years versus the number of sex workers arrested?

sentences.speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Is increasing the present penalty of $10,000 to $100,000 sufficient in deterring these offences?

sections.label: Conditional immunity for victimised women
sections.summary: The speaker urges the Minister to consider conditional immunity from charges like soliciting and conditional protection from blacklisting for victimised women, similar to the certificate of cooperation for drug traffickers.

sentences.speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: The analysis further offers that the Bill "simply prioritises...health and safety of people engaged in sex work, including human trafficking victims, over their criminalisation...for misdemeanor ...when this population comes forward as victims or witnesses of specified violent crimes." Mr Speaker, I urge the Minister to consider offering these victimised women conditional immunity from charges like soliciting and conditional protection from blacklisting to join us in our fight against exploitative agents, similar in principle to the certificate of cooperation given to drug traffickers.

sections.label: Criminal compensation for exploited women
sections.summary: The speaker asks if working with the Court to arrange criminal compensation for exploited women can be considered, noting the Court must consider compensation under section 359.

sentences.speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: If we send them away with debt, we are implicitly pushing them to re-enter into risky business arrangements and fall prey to other dangerous agents.

sentences.speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: I seek the Minister's clarification if we could consider working closely with the Court to arrange for criminal compensation for the exploited women.

sentences.speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: The Court is obliged to actively consider whether or not to order compensation under section 359 of the Criminal Procedure Code.

sections.label: AWARE on women's autonomy
sections.summary: AWARE notes that upholding women's autonomy and agency, including sex workers', is crucial to gender equality as defined by CEDAW.

sentences.speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: The Association of Women for Action and Research (AWARE), Singapore’s leading gender equality advocacy group notes that upholding women’s autonomy and agency, including that of sex workers, is crucial to respecting, protecting and fulfilling our commitment to gender equality as defined by the UN Convention on Elimination of Discrimination Against Women (CEDAW).

sections.label: Prostitution not a crime
sections.summary: Prostitution per se is not a crime in Singapore.

sentences.speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: Prostitution per se is not a crime in Singapore.

sections.label: Landlords' leasing diligence duty
sections.summary: Clause 12 amendments to section 148 clarify that landlords and their appointed agents must perform reasonable diligence when leasing premises to tenants.

sentences.speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: The amendments in clause 12 for section 148 has now clarified that landlords and/or their appointed agents need to perform reasonable diligence when leasing premises out to tenants.

sections.label: Powers against overseas vice operators
sections.summary: Clause 10 amendments to section 146A give authorities greater power to prosecute and enforce against overseas operators of vice services using remote communications to facilitate commercial sexual services in Singapore.

sentences.speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: The amendments in clause 10 for section 146A have given the authorities greater power to prosecute and undertake enforcement actions against overseas operators of vice services who use remote communications channels to facilitate the provision of commercial sexual services in Singapore.

sections.label: Higher penalties for trafficking
sections.summary: Amendments to clauses 3, 4 and 5 increase penalties for trafficking women and girls and importing them under false pretence for prostitution, serving as strong deterrence.

sentences.speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: The amendments to clauses 3, 4 and 5 that increase the penalty of offence in trafficking women and girls and to import them under the false pretence with the intent that they be employed or used for the purpose of prostitution either within or outside Singapore will certainly serve as strong deterrence to would-be offenders.

sections.label: Extraterritorial jurisdiction and social media
sections.summary: The speaker supports the Bill and asks what measures the Ministry will take to enlist social media providers' cooperation.

sentences.speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: It is with these two aspects that I conclude my speech in firm support of the Bill.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: I commend the Ministry's efforts to deal with this problem through the introduction of extraterritorial jurisdiction to the Charter.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: What measures will the Ministry implement to enlist the cooperation of social media providers to help deter such offers and bring those involved to task?

sections.label: Mitigations for innocent owners
sections.summary: The speaker asks what other mitigations exist for unfortunate, innocent owners.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: What other mitigations are there for the unfortunate, innocent owners?

sections.label: Framework for victim-prostitutes
sections.summary: The speaker asks whether a framework exists for victim-prostitutes to seek assistance and act as witnesses.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: Do we have a framework to enable victim-prostitutes to seek assistance and also act as witnesses?

sections.label: Owners' knowledge of vice activities
sections.summary: MHA stated owners and tenants must show they had no knowledge and could not with reasonable diligence have known of vice use.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: MHA has stated that if vice activities are detected at their premises, home owners and tenants will have to show that they had no knowledge of and could not, with "reasonable diligence", have known that the place would be used for vice activities.

sections.label: Wong Kan Seng's 1999 warning
sections.summary: The speaker recalls supporting the Massage Establishments Bill and quotes Mr Wong Kan Seng's 1999 warning against driving prostitution underground.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Two years ago, I stood in this House to support the Massage Establishments Bill.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: But in that speech, I said, "Worse still, we might drive these activities further underground." This was the fear of former Home Affairs Minister, Mr Wong Kan Seng, who said this in Parliament in 1999 in relation to a question about prostitution, "It is better that the Police know where these areas are and enforcement action can be taken, rather than to disperse these brothels to the whole of Singapore and we have a cat-and-mouse game chasing after them or, worse still, drive them underground, and they will be operating everywhere." I fear that we are doing what Mr Wong advised us 20 years ago not to do and that the cat-and-mouse game has started.

sections.label: Smaller parlours harder to apprehend
sections.summary: Interviews with massage workers showed proliferation because smaller parlours were harder to apprehend for sexual services, and the speaker asks the end goal.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: From interviews with massage workers, the proliferation was also because smaller parlours were harder to apprehend for sexual services." What is our end goal?

sections.label: Evolving vice activities cat-and-mouse game
sections.summary: The passage states that vice activities are evolving partly because of our actions, and this cat-and-mouse game wastes resources and leaves us one step behind.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: However, it seems that the vice activities are evolving at least partly because of our actions.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: This cat-and-mouse game means that we are wasting our precious resources and, most importantly, we are always one step behind.

sections.label: MHA study and US laws
sections.summary: The passage asks whether MHA is studying the problem and what others are doing, noting US states passed laws letting sex workers report crimes without fear of arrest.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: However, can I ask if MHA is studying this problem and also studying what others are doing?

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: I understand that in the US states of California, Utah and Washington, laws have been passed to allow sex workers to, without fear of arrest or prosecution, report crimes that they were victims of or witnesses to.

sections.label: Non-profit groups helping sex workers
sections.summary: The passage states Singapore has non-profit groups providing social, emotional and legal support for sex workers, and hopes for Government funding for The Next Step Programme.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: The fortunate thing in Singapore is that, in Singapore, we do have non-profit groups helping these women.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: It provides social, emotional and legal support for sex workers in Singapore, and it hopes to launch The Next Step Programme, to which I hope the Government can provide some funding and support.

sections.label: Sex workers leaving and Josephine Teo
sections.summary: The passage states research shows sex workers who left for at least two years did so after about six attempts, and quotes Minister Josephine Teo on help available.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Research shows that sex workers who have successfully left and abstained from sex work for at least two years have been able to do so only after about six attempts on average.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: In 2017, Minister Josephine Teo said in relation to sex workers, "For those who wish to transit to other types of work, I appreciate it really may not be easy for them, but help is available and we are most willing to reach out to them".

sections.label: Women's Charter landlord responsibilities
sections.summary: The passage welcomes proposed amendments to the Women's Charter to increase landlords' responsibilities to verify tenants' identities, background and purpose of renting.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yee Chia Hsing (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: (In Mandarin)  : 	Mr Speaker, Sir, I welcome the proposed amendments to the Women’s Charter to increase the responsibilities for landlords.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yee Chia Hsing (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: The landlords have a duty to verify the identities of potential tenants, their background and the purpose of renting.

sections.label: Landlord and HDB flat owner questions
sections.summary: The passage asks whether landlords are responsible if a tenant later lets others stay without their knowledge, and whether HDB flat owners can rely on property agents' advice.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yee Chia Hsing (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: First, will the landlords be held responsible if the original tenant subsequently allows others to stay in the premises without their knowledge?

sentences.speaker: Mr Yee Chia Hsing (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Second, can the HDB flat owners rely on the advice of the property agents?

sections.label: Online listings of sexual services
sections.summary: A search of an online forum yielded over 1,800 listings offering massage and sexual services, mostly by foreign nationals on social visit visas in discreet apartments.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: As of last week, a simple search of such services on an infamous online forum easily yielded over 1,800 listings that offer massage and sexual services, mostly by foreign nationals here on social visit visas, in various "discreet apartments" across Singapore.

sections.label: Extraterritorial jurisdiction enforcement question
sections.summary: Amendments to the Women's Charter introduce extraterritorial jurisdiction to section 146A, and the speaker asks how this will be feasibly enforced.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: With the constant evolution of such digital platforms, it is crucial that our enforcement officers be updated regularly on the latest technologies that are being used to circumvent the detection of vice syndicates in Singapore.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: I am, therefore, happy to see that the proposed amendments to the Women’s Charter have introduced extraterritorial jurisdiction to section 146A.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: While this plugs a legal gap by allowing the Police to take decisive action against any overseas person using remote communication services to facilitate the provision of sexual services in Singapore, I would like to ask how will this be feasibly enforced?

sections.label: Safe reporting channel for exploited women
sections.summary: The passage calls for a safe reporting channel for exploited women and cites a US State Department report of 16 trafficking cases in Singapore in 2018.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: Lastly, we must not forget about providing a safe reporting channel to the women who have been exploited and forced to work as sex workers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: I read with concern about a report published by the US State Department earlier this year, which claimed that there were 16 trafficking cases in Singapore in 2018, of which 10 involved sex trafficking.

sections.label: Singapore's pragmatic approach to vice
sections.summary: Singapore takes a pragmatic approach to vice, prioritising preventing organised crime groups from gaining a foothold and addressing public nuisance from vice activities.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
sentences.text: The experiences of these countries are mixed, but what Mr Wong Kan Seng said 20 years ago and which Mr Louis Ng quoted, still holds true: no country has successfully eradicated prostitution.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
sentences.text: In Singapore, we take a pragmatic approach towards vice.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
sentences.text: We prioritise our efforts by: (a) ensuring organised crime groups and syndicates do not gain a foothold through vice activities; and (b) addressing public nuisance caused by vice-related activities, such as soliciting in public and vice in the heartlands.

sections.label: Upstream targeting of vice platforms
sections.summary: Upstream efforts target platforms that may facilitate vice by taking down vice websites, regulating entertainment and massage outlets, and deterring foreigners seeking sex work.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
sentences.text: Upstream, we target platforms which may be used to facilitate vice activities by: (a)	taking down and blocking vice websites as and when they are detected; (b)	establishing a regulatory regime for public entertainment and massage establishment outlets, which may be fronts for vice activities; and (c)	detecting and deterring foreigners seeking to enter Singapore for sex work.

sections.label: Arrests for vice and immigration offences
sections.summary: Between 2016 and 2018, about 8,800 foreign females were arrested for vice and immigration offences, and 328 vice abettors were arrested.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
sentences.text: Between 2016 and 2018, about 8,800 foreign females were arrested for vice and immigration offences.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
sentences.text: In the same period, 328 vice abettors were arrested.

sections.label: Police found no trafficking cases
sections.summary: Police investigations found none of the 10 alleged sex trafficking cases was substantiated as trafficking under PHTA.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
sentences.text: Subsequent investigations by the Police ascertained that none of the 10 alleged sex trafficking cases was substantiated as trafficking under PHTA.

sections.label: Section 146A arrest amendments
sections.summary: Amendments to section 146A allow arrest of offenders entering Singapore even if overseas when the offence was committed.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
sentences.text: With the amendments to section 146A, we will be able to arrest offenders when they enter Singapore, even if they were overseas at the point of commission of the offence.

sections.label: Syndicates liable under section 146A
sections.summary: Amendments make syndicates using social media to advertise sexual services liable even if server or poster is overseas.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
sentences.text: With these amendments to section 146A, syndicates which use these social media and social messaging platforms to advertise or facilitate the provision of sexual services in Singapore, will be liable for an offence, even if the server is overseas, or even if the person posting the advertisement is overseas.

sections.label: Maximum penalties considered from other laws
sections.summary: Maximum penalties took into account other legislation such as PHTA, which carries a $100,000 fine, 10 years' imprisonment and caning.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
sentences.text: In determining the appropriate maximum penalties, we took into account the penalties in other relevant legislations, such as the PHTA, which also carries a maximum fine of $100,000, imprisonment of up to 10 years, and caning, even for first-time offenders.

sections.label: Owner liability for brothel use
sections.summary: Owners or master tenants who reasonably ascertain premises will not be used as a brothel are not liable if it later is.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
sentences.text: At the point of signing the lease agreement or releasing the premises for occupation to a tenant, if the property owner or master tenant had done what was reasonably possible to ascertain that the premises are not going to be used as a brothel, the owner or master tenant will not be liable for an offence even if the unit is subsequently used as a brothel.

sections.label: Clause 12(b) tenant amendment
sections.summary: The amendment in clause 12(b) of the Bill makes it harder for a tenant or occupant to turn a blind eye.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
sentences.text: The latter is an amendment in clause 12(b) in the Bill, which will make it harder for a tenant or occupant to turn a blind eye.

sections.label: Property agents and legislative changes
sections.summary: The Government is working with CEA so property agents know the legislative changes and follow guidelines helping owners and tenants meet reasonable diligence requirements.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
sentences.text: Property agents play an important role in helping home owners and tenants comply with the law.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
sentences.text: We are, therefore, working with CEA to ensure that property agents are aware of these legislative changes and to introduce professional guidelines to ensure that property agents help owners and tenants meet these reasonable diligence requirements.

sections.label: Short-term rental platforms responsibility
sections.summary: The owner and tenant of the property-in-use remain responsible for the reasonable diligence requirements under section 148 of the Women's Charter.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
sentences.text: To Mr Melvin Yong’s question on the use of short-term rental platforms, the owner and tenant of the property-in-use are still responsible for the reasonable diligence requirements under section 148 of the Women’s Charter.

sections.label: Mentally defective term and vice activities
sections.summary: The term "mentally defective" will be looked into in subsequent Women's Charter reviews, and the Bill enhances action against vice activities and protects neighbourhoods.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
sentences.text: One final point, to Ms Anthea Ong's comment on the use of the term "mentally defective", I acknowledge her point and we will look into this in subsequent reviews of the Women's Charter.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
sentences.text: The Bill is needed to enhance our ability to deal effectively against vice activities of syndicates and individuals, especially those operating online, and to ensure better protection for our neighbourhoods from vice activities.

sections.label: Abolitionist route for prostitution
sections.summary: The Member asks whether the Ministry would consider an abolitionist route like France, Sweden and Iceland to criminalise clients but offer sex workers an escape route.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alex Yam
sentences.text: Prostitution is no different, brings with it sexual violence, organised crime and other after-effects.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alex Yam
sentences.text: I, therefore, ask if the Ministry would consider adopting an abolitionist route as adopted by France, Sweden and Iceland to criminalise the punters, the clients, but offer an escape route for a better life for those who are in this trade.

sections.label: Concerns about criminalising sex
sections.summary: Studies assessed data changes reflected policing practice and sex work organisation, and there are grave concerns criminalising sex drives clients and sex workers underground.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
sentences.text: Some studies have assessed that any change in data simply reflected changes in policing practice and the way in which sex work is organised.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
sentences.text: We mentioned earlier, and some of the other Members have also mentioned, we do have grave concerns that by criminalising sex, we drive clients and sex workers underground and we make it harder for sex workers to protect themselves or for social workers to reach them.

sections.label: No prosecution of Singaporean sex workers
sections.summary: Singaporean sex workers are not prosecuted for providing sexual services because it is not an offence, and policies help them transit out of sex work.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
sentences.text: On the first point that the Member mentioned, I would like to clarify that we actually do not prosecute Singaporean sex workers for sex offences, for providing sexual services, because it is not an offence.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
sentences.text: On the second point about transiting out of sex work, I mentioned that we have various policies in place and this is something that the Government will also look into actively to help Singaporean sex workers transit out of the sex trade.
